from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Leap: From Geometry to Abstraction", lecture_lines)

        self.place_in_area(vector_arrow, "B4", "C6", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Create(vector_arrow))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF00FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transform vector into an abstract dot on a coordinate plane #00FFFF.
        dot = Dot(color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(dot, "D5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(vector_arrow, dot))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Flash the dot to emphasize abstraction of location [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/arrow.svg] #FFFFFF.
        # Reuse arrow asset as an abstract visual indicator, scaled down.
        abstract_symbol = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/arrow.svg", color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(abstract_symbol, "D5", scale_factor=0.4)
        
        self.play(Flash(dot, color="#FFFFFF", flash_radius=0.5))
        self.add(abstract_symbol)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", [
            "Vector Spaces unify diverse mathematical structures.",
            "We apply linear algebra tools across many fields.",
            "Data science and quantum mechanics rely on these rules."
        ])
        
        # Animation Elements
        axiom_list = VGroup(*[\
            Text(f"Axiom {i+1}", font_size=24, color="#00FF00") 
            for i in range(8)
        ]).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        
        # Load asset
        computer_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/computer.svg")
        check = Tex(r"$\checkmark$", color="#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        # Using grid B3-E5 per feedback (Issue 35/50)
        self.place_in_area(axiom_list, 'B3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.55)
        # Tether computer icon to axiom_list (B011)
        computer_icon.next_to(axiom_list, RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(axiom_list), FadeIn(computer_icon))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Using grid E4 per feedback (Issue 34/49)
        self.place_at_grid(check, 'E4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(check))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(FadeOut(axiom_list), FadeOut(check), FadeOut(computer_icon), FadeOut(self.title), FadeOut(self.lecture))
        self.wait(1)

sections.title: The Leap: From Geometry to Abstraction (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Brief review of physical vectors (arrows in 2D/3D). Introduce the idea that 'vectors' don't have to be arrows—they can be any objects (functions, polynomials, matrices) that obey specific structural rules.
sections.example: Visualizing a 2D arrow vs. a 'vector' representing the pitch and rhythm of a bird's song.

sections.title: The Foundation: The Two Core Operations (0:45-1:45)
sections.content: Explain that a space is 'vectorial' only if it supports two operations: Vector Addition and Scalar Multiplication. Use a split-screen animation showing geometric arrows on one side and algebraic polynomials on the other.
sections.example: Adding two polynomials (x + 1) + (2x + 3) = 3x + 4, mirroring how we add arrows head-to-tail.

sections.title: The Eight Axioms: The Rules of the Game (1:45-3:15)
sections.content: A high-speed visual walkthrough of the 8 axioms (Closure, Associativity, Commutativity, Zero vector, Inverse, etc.). Use an 'ingredient list' graphic to show that as long as these 8 laws are satisfied, the set is a Vector Space.
sections.example: A 'Robot Factory' analogy: If the robot's logic system follows these 8 laws, it can exist in the Vector Space, regardless of whether its 'limbs' are numbers or functions.

sections.title: Non-Example: Detecting Broken Spaces (3:15-4:15)
sections.content: Critical knowledge point: Show why a set that doesn't include the Zero vector or fails closure under addition cannot be a vector space. Use a visual 'gate' animation where invalid objects are rejected.
sections.example: A set of arrows restricted to only the first quadrant—addition is fine, but scalar multiplication by a negative number 'escapes' the set, breaking the space.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis (4:15-5:00)
sections.content: Wrap up by emphasizing that abstraction allows us to apply linear algebra tools (bases, dimensions, transformations) to complex fields like Data Science and Quantum Mechanics.
sections.example: The 'Universal Toolkit' metaphor: One set of mathematical laws (Vector Spaces) applied to everything from Spotify’s music recommendation algorithms to a cat’s movement simulation.
